2. Let O be the origin and A be the point $\mathrm{z}_{1}=1+2 i$. If B is the point $\mathrm{z}_{2}, \operatorname{Re}\left(\mathrm{z}_{2}\right)<0$, such that OAB is a right angled isosceles triangle with OB as hypotenuse, then which of the following is NOT true ?
(A) $\arg \mathrm{z}_{2}=\pi-\tan ^{-1} 3$
(B) $\arg \left(\mathrm{z}_{1}-2 \mathrm{z}_{2}\right)=-\tan ^{-1} \frac{4}{3}$
(C) $\left|\mathrm{z}_{2}\right|=\sqrt{10}$
(D) $\left|2 \mathrm{z}_{1}-\mathrm{z}_{2}\right|=5$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{AO} . \mathrm{z}^{-i \pi / 2}=-2+i$
So $\mathrm{OB}=(-2+i)+(1+2 i)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{z}_{2}=-1+3 i \\
\therefore\left|2 \mathrm{z}_{1}-\mathrm{z}_{2}\right|=\sqrt{10}
\end{array}$$
3. If the system of linear equations.
$$\begin{array}{l}
8 x+y+4 z=-2 \\
x+y+z=0 \\
\lambda x-3 y=\mu
\end{array}$$
has infinitely many solutions, then the distance of the point $\left(\lambda, \mu,-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ from the plane $8 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+4 \mathrm{z}+ 2=0$ is :
(A) $3 \sqrt{5}$
(B) 4
(C) $\frac{26}{9}$
(D) $\frac{10}{3}$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)

Sol. $\mathrm{D}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}8 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \lambda & -3 & 0\end{array}\right|=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=4$
Also $\mathrm{D}_{1}=\mathrm{D}_{2}=\mathrm{D}_{3}=0$
So $\mu=-2$
Point $\left(4,-2,-\frac{1}{2}\right)$
Distance from plane $=\frac{10}{3}$
4. Let A be a $2 \times 2$ matrix with $\operatorname{det}(\mathrm{A})=-1$ and $\operatorname{det} ((\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{I})(\operatorname{Adj}(\mathrm{A})+\mathrm{I}))=4$. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of A can be :
(A) -1
(B) 2
(C) 1
(D) $-\sqrt{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Let $\mathrm{A}=\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{a} & \mathrm{b} \\ \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{d}\end{array}\right] ; \mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}=-1$
$$\begin{array}{l}
|\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{I}||\operatorname{adj} \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{I}|=4 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}+\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}+1=2 \text { or }-2 \\
\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}=2 \text { or }-2
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are $\alpha$ and $\frac{\alpha}{3}$ respectively. If $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=1)=\frac{4}{243}$, then $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=4$ or 5$)$ is equal to :

Let $\mathrm{E}_{1}, \mathrm{E}_{2}, \mathrm{E}_{3}$ be three mutually exclusive events such that $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right)=\frac{2+3 \mathrm{p}}{6}, \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{2-\mathrm{p}}{8}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{3}\right) =\frac{1-\mathrm{p}}{2}$. If the maximum and minimum values of p are $\mathrm{p}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{p}_{2}$, then $\left(\mathrm{p}_{1}+\mathrm{p}_{2}\right)$ is equal to :
(A) $\frac{2}{3}$
(B) $\frac{5}{3}$
(D)

options.D:
7

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\quad \vec{a} \times \vec{b}=(1-\alpha) \hat{i}+\left(\alpha^{2}-2\right) \hat{j}+(\alpha-2) \hat{k}$
Projection of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}$ on $-\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\frac{(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot(-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k})}{3}=30 \\
\Rightarrow 2 \alpha^{2}-\alpha-91=0 \\
\Rightarrow \alpha=7,-\frac{13}{2}
\end{array}$$
16. The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are $\alpha$ and $\frac{\alpha}{3}$ respectively. If $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=1)=\frac{4}{243}$, then $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=4$ or 5$)$ is equal to :
(A) $\frac{5}{9}$
(B) $\frac{64}{81}$
(C) $\frac{16}{27}$
(D) $\frac{145}{243}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\mathrm{np}=\alpha$
$$\mathrm{npq}=\alpha / 3$$

From (1) \& (2)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{q}=1 / 3 \& \mathrm{p}=2 / 3 \\
{ }^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{C}_{1} \mathrm{q}^{\mathrm{n}-1} \mathrm{p}^{1}=\frac{4}{243} \\
\frac{\mathrm{n}}{3^{\mathrm{n}}}=\frac{2}{243} \\
\mathrm{n}=6 \\
\mathrm{P}(4 \text { or } 5)={ }^{6} \mathrm{C}_{4}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{4}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}+{ }^{6} \mathrm{C}_{5}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{5} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{0} \\
=\frac{16}{27}
\end{array}$$

Let $\mathrm{E}_{1}, \mathrm{E}_{2}, \mathrm{E}_{3}$ be three mutually exclusive events such that $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right)=\frac{2+3 \mathrm{p}}{6}, \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)=\frac{2-\mathrm{p}}{8}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{3}\right) =\frac{1-\mathrm{p}}{2}$. If the maximum and minimum values of p are $\mathrm{p}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{p}_{2}$, then $\left(\mathrm{p}_{1}+\mathrm{p}_{2}\right)$ is equal to :
(A) $\frac{2}{3}$
(B) $\frac{5}{3}$
(D) 1

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $0 \leq \mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{i}\right) \leq 1$ for $\mathrm{i}=1,2,3$
$$\Rightarrow-2 / 3 \leq \mathrm{p} \leq 1$$
$\mathrm{E}_{1} \& \mathrm{E}_{2} \& \mathrm{E}_{3}$ are mutually exclusive
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{1}\right)+\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{2}\right)+\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{E}_{3}\right) \leq 1 \\
\Rightarrow 2 / 3 \leq \mathrm{p} \leq 1 \\
\mathrm{p}_{1}=1, \mathrm{p}_{2}=2 / 3 \\
\mathrm{p}_{1}+\mathrm{p}_{2}=5 / 3
\end{array}$$
